subject: Discovery recap: tool calling & structured output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha.chen@northforge.ai>, Aiden Brooks <aiden.b@northforge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: tool calling & structured output requirements

Hi Samantha / Aiden —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Per our discussion, here’s a short recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Agent outputs are currently inconsistent between prompts (field names, ordering, optional fields).
- Downstream systems require a deterministic JSON schema for ingestion. Manual post-processing is brittle and expensive.
- Occasional hallucinated fields and missing required keys are causing downstream rejections.
- Latency spikes during peak time (observed 95th percentile > 600ms) leading to user-facing delays.

Current stack
- Node backend calling multiple agent models (in-house + open models) running on EKS.
- Post-processing service (Python) attempts to normalize outputs before ingestion.
- Compliance: PII redaction is currently handled client-side in a separate pipeline.

Success criteria you described
- Deterministic, schema-adherent JSON output from the agent (fields present, stable keys, validated types).
- Structured output validation pass rate > 99% on pilot dataset.
- Inference latency <= 250ms p95 for single-turn tool calls in production config (pilot target).
- Clear escalation path and instrumentation for regressions.

Recommendations / suggested approach
1) Define canonical JSON schema for primary agent responses (attached example-schema.json).
2) Implement a structured-output mode + strict validation at the model/runtime boundary to enforce formatting.
3) Run an initial pilot with 10k representative prompts to measure schema pass rate and latency.
4) Technical deep-dive with your engineering team (30–45m) to align on integration points (batching, tool-calling, retry semantics).

Attachments
- example-schema.json (attached) — baseline schema we can iterate on.
- redwood-pilot-proposal.pdf (attached) — pilot scope + resourcing estimate.

Next steps
- Samantha: please confirm the dataset (or share a sample of ~200 prompts) that we can use for the pilot.
- Dev: can you lead the technical deep-dive? Suggested times: Thu Aug 26 (10–11am PT) or Fri Aug 27 (2–3pm PT).
- Marissa: I’ll loop you in on pricing/SOW once we confirm pilot scope.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool calling & structured output requirements

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this captures the problems well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Schema expectations
- The schema needs to include a stable top-level "response" object with the following required fields: "intent_id", "entities[]" (list), "confidence_score" (float), and an optional "actions[]" array for tool calls.
- We cannot accept free-text top-level keys — ordering and key names must be deterministic.

2) Compliance
- Any PII (emails, phone numbers, SSNs) must be redacted before persistence. We’d like the redaction to happen in the runtime layer if possible.

3) Integration constraints
- Our ingestion pipeline will validate JSON strictly; any schema validation failure will be sent to a quarantine queue (manual review).

4) Pilot dataset
- I can share 300 labeled prompts and examples that represent the most common user flows. I’ll attach our agent-workflow-overview.pdf so you can see current routing and fallback behaviors.

Meeting — Thu Aug 26 10am PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite and include the technical folks who will own the runtime and validation.

One more ask: could you provide a short example of the strict-validation behavior (pseudocode + expected responses) so our engs can review ahead of the call?

Best,
Samantha
Head of Product Integrations | NorthForge AI
samantha.chen@northforge.ai

Samantha —

Appreciate the clarifications — all good. I’ve attached a short pseudocode example below that we’ll expand into a runnable example for the call.

PSEUDOCODE (validation flow)
1) model_response = call_model(prompt, mode="structured")
2) if validate_json_schema(model_response, canonical_schema):
     return model_response
   else:
     if can_retry_with_stricter_prompt():
       model_response = call_model(prompt + "\nINSTRUCTIONS: Return valid JSON adhering to schema XYZ. Do not add extra keys.", retries=2)
       if validate_json_schema(model_response, canonical_schema):
         return model_response
     send_to_quarantine(model_response, reason="schema_failure")
     return {"error":"schema_validation_failed", "diagnostic": summarize_failures(model_response)}

For the call on Thu Aug 26 10am PT I’ll add Dev (runtime lead) and Marissa (commercial). Please confirm attendee emails and I’ll send the invite.

Action items for the call
- Agree canonical schema and edge-case handling rules (optional fields, null vs empty arrays).
- Validate redaction approach for PII (runtime vs pre-processing).
- Define pilot success metrics and test dataset.

Thanks — I’ll send the calendar invite after you confirm.

Jordan
